observation: The work package whose whole purpose was 'no fixture arranges a state production cannot produce' shipped eight of exactly that violation into review. framework/db/src/__tests__/schema.integration.test.ts had eight bare insert(teams) with no teamMembers companion (pre-fix :73,136,159,190,221,268,582,600). Three things hid them at once: the detector's write set is FILE-grained (crossing-detectors.ts:779-783), so the one pre-existing companion write at :115 credited every site in the file and governance-lint reported 0 development violations; schema-test-decision.md:162 recorded this file as '4 sites (438, 461, 474, 486)' — only the four lint-VISIBLE knowledgeItems sites — so the decision doc itself never enumerated the teams entities; and architecture C6 named the laundering hazard explicitly ('one companion write anywhere in a file silences every site in that file... this plan forbids exploiting it') without any check that per-entity completion happened. It survived six architecture critique rounds. What found it: a reviewer reading the diff entity by entity against C6 instead of reading the lint output (review.md B1).

The per-entity checker written to close B1 was sanity-broken instead of asserted: schema.integration.test.ts was reverted to its pre-fix content at 736dfa9e, the checker re-run, and it named exactly the same eight sites at exactly the eight lines the reviewer had derived by hand — then the file was restored and the diff confirmed only the eight companion inserts were new. Both the PASS run and the FAIL run are committed to probes/per-entity-companion-check-output.txt. A checker that has only ever printed PASS is indistinguishable from one that cannot fail.

The round-2 reviewer attacked the builder's own checker rather than trusting its PASS. It enumerated four blind spots from the source (only bare-identifier test()/it() callees are walked, so 31 owner inserts in the touched set are unseen — 30 inside named file-local seed helpers and one at module top level, ah6-test-server.ts:115; helper calls not literally named seedTeam/seedKnowledgeItem/seedBase credit nothing; `written` is a Set so presence not count; test.each/.skip/.only are PropertyAccessExpression callees and invisible) and then established the conclusion three independent stronger ways: per-function count balance over 30 owner-writing functions, whole-file owner-vs-companion totals, and per-scope count balance with helper credits counted per call. Plus a sweep of the 34 non-touched local modules the touched files import, for laundering through an untouched helper. Zero unbalanced on every axis. The conclusion was true; the evidence the builder cited did not reach it.

A self-caused test failure was reported as pre-existing because the comparison baseline was the branch's own commit. An intermediate test:full run showed 6192/1, framework/db/src/__tests__/governance-model.test.ts:178 asserting 114 development-allowed rules. The git-stash comparison used to classify it ran against this worktree's HEAD (736dfa9e), which already carried this strand's own T7 commit 27ccc8b8 — the commit that flips two decided-rules.json rows to development: allowed and moves the true count from 114/10 to 116/8. Against origin/main the failure is unambiguously this branch's. Caught by the coordinator, not by the builder; fixed by recomputing from live governance/decided-rules.json via jq and pinning 116/8 with the reason in a comment, then sweeping the other two governance test files for the same class of stale count (none — they build synthetic censuses).

A gate result was written into the record from expectation while the gate was actually red. progress.json asserted 'knip and knip:production unaffected (byte-identical to pre-change baseline)'; no knip probe existed in probes/. In fact commit 23eb1658 (T5) removed the only importers of @electric-sql/pglite and drizzle-orm from layers/core-ui and of @electric-sql/pglite from tools/eval, orphaning three manifest declarations: `npm run knip` exit 1 and `npm run deps:check` exit 1 — both chained in verify, so the branch could not have merged. Found by the reviewer running the gates rather than reading the record (review.md B2/B3). knip:production was genuinely clean, which is what made the sentence feel true.

A probe's reach was generalised in the record beyond what the script walks. The B1 entry claimed the per-entity checker established 'zero unbalanced entities anywhere in the diff'; the checker only walks bare test()/it() bodies and is blind to 31 owner inserts in the same diff. The probe's own header and PASS line were correctly hedged ('inside one test(...)/it(...) scope') — only the progress record over-reached. Caught on the second review pass (review.md R2-D1). Together with the census-pin misattribution and the knip claim, three claims in this run outran their evidence and all three leaned the same way: confident exactly where the measurement did not reach. Two were caught by reviewers, one by the coordinator; none by the agent that wrote it.

The central evidence for the deletion AC was a search that could not fail. AC-5' proved the bookkeeping mechanism gone with `rg` over scripts/ governance/ ... — and scripts/rules/crossings.ts holds a literal NUL byte at offset 3084 (line 64, a raw \0 as a site separator inside a template literal), so ripgrep classifies it as binary and silently skips it. Measured in critique round 5 B2 and reproduced in round 6: the same token set gives rg -n 39 hits with ZERO from crossings.ts vs git grep -na 43 with 4 from it, while baselineRatchet is defined at :105 and compareBaseline called at :115. The proof would have read 'clean closure' with the ratchet fully intact, for the one file that mattered most — and the blindness is self-referential, lifting only once the block holding the NUL is deleted. CLAUDE.md warns about this exact hazard by name. Closed by switching to `git grep -na` (also tracked-file-bounded, so untracked scratch cannot pad the count) and by requiring a positive control BEFORE the deletion.

Positive-control-before-deletion became the shape of the deletion proof, not a nicety. The plan published the exact expected control output — 78 lines across 20 files, with scripts/rules/crossings.ts at 7 hits, governance/misplaced-files.json at 1, sibling plans at 6/4/4 — and instructed the builder to STOP if the search missed any of them, because a search that cannot see the residue before deletion proves nothing after. Both runs are committed: probes/residue-search-positive-control.txt (78 lines) and probes/residue-search-after.txt (exactly one hit, the named permitted governance-lint.test.ts:641). The same discipline was applied to the red phase of D9' case 3 (observed red against a tree where readyToFlip does not exist yet) and to the bite proof.

The founder reversed a design decision of their own from one work package earlier, mid-build. AU28 Ruling 2 asked for a mechanical shrink-only ratchet (governance/baseline.json); Ruling E removes it — 'what weird linter is this that checks against a record?' The stated trigger is having watched it run: a red build as the reward for fixing violations, naming no architectural fact. The reversal arrived after the build had already reached 27ccc8b8 and had already cleared the development world to zero, and it rebased the remaining task list onto work the plan never contained: governance/rule-severity.json, a new no-per-file-allowances rule (186 lines) with overlay + standalone attack cases, deletion of baseline.json + the generator + --adopt + the baseline-ratchet rule + 12 ratchet tests + crossing-report.ts, and a residue sweep across docs and three sibling plans. It also rewrote two ACs (4 and 5) and made the deletion unconditional and owned by this WP instead of falling to whichever of four siblings finished last.

A critique round was overruled rather than adjudicated, and the overrule expanded scope into production code. Round 3's blocking B1 argued the rework conflated 'production never performs this operation' with Ruling B's 'test cannot fail', and that deleting nine live constraint tests would remove the only executable guard on seven shipped schema properties (six of the nine clear zero lint sites). Escalated to the founder, who recorded Ruling D: the tests go, AND if a mechanism exists that nothing production reaches, delete the whole feature — explicitly amending plan.md's 'the production world entirely' out-of-scope line. The removal branch then came back EMPTY: no deletion mechanism exists in code for any of the five row shapes, verified two independent ways in round 4 (code-primitive enumeration, plus schema structure — the five tables carry only RESTRICT FKs or none, so no cascade chain of any depth reaches their rows). Final tally: 0 production files changed, no migration, no FK or onDelete touched. The one reachable case found (teamMembers via deleteTeam from the POST /teams rollback) was kept, and its two tests kept, exactly as the ruling required.

The planner declined part of a critique finding and was right. Round-6 B4 called both clauses of .pipeline/work/AU30/plan.md:28 false. The planner corrected the first ('the ratchet records progress' — gone) and KEPT the second ('no rule promotes until the last one lands'), re-grounded on a different and still-true reason: the group key carries no table name (service -> db:table (unowned) [table:write] production, all six unowned tables under it), so the key cannot leave rule-severity.json until every table is owned. Recorded with the reason it matters (architecture.md:603): restating the clause as 'each rule promotes as it goes' would have contradicted AU30/plan.md:7 and .pipeline/AU.md:29, two lines that are correct today and after this PR. It also declined the tokens `ratchet` and `promot` for the residue search with the measurement showing why, and stated AU30:28's unreachability by any honest token as a limit instead of papering over it.

Actually executing a live proof found a pre-existing runtime break that no test covered and that reading the code would not have surfaced. Booting layers/core-ui/__scripts__/ah6-test-server.ts for the mandated ready-line evidence produced DrizzleQueryError with an empty SET clause (probes/ah6-orig-boot.log): the assistant seed wrote harnessType/modelId/modelProvider/systemPrompt/maxConcurrentSessions onto users, columns that had moved to agentRunConfig. Fixed bounded to the one seed with @lore. The reviewer also caught that probes/ah1-boot.log was 0 bytes and ran the lane itself (ready line + GET /api/teams -> 401 with the auth middleware live) — a live-proof list is only evidence if someone checks the artifacts are non-empty.

A test that cannot fail was proposed INSIDE the work package whose own Ruling B bans them, and caught only in critique round 5 (B3). D9' case 3 was specified as a unit over crossingRules asserting that a 'warn' key with zero live violations produces no error — but crossingRules.evaluate maps over myViolations (crossings.ts:82-94), so a zero-violation key emits nothing by construction, whatever the severity map says. Green before, green after, green under every implementation of the forbidden check. Withdrawn rather than shipped as AC evidence, replaced with readyToFlip, which is falsifiable on three axes (invert the predicate, drop the report, name the wrong key) and was observed red before T8 existed. The prohibition it was meant to pin is now held by a return type (readonly string[], not Finding[], so it cannot carry severity), a README prohibition, and review — disclosed as such rather than claimed as automated.

One directory was read as the whole development world and it made an unreachable branch look viable. Feasibility P23 said 'all five development files that insert teams'; the real figure is 178 (git grep -l 'insert(teams)' -- '*__tests__*'), and ZERO of them lack a teamMembers mention (round 6 N1). The conclusion the claim supported was actually stronger than stated — the trap is universal, not confined to framework/db/src/__tests__ — but D12's fallback ('append to an existing fixture whose write set contains no teamMembers') reads as an option with a searchable precondition when on the live tree the qualifying set is empty. Retained only as the diagnosis for a builder who tries it.

A gate the plan named for leftover exports does not gate them. D8'/P19e cited knip and knip:production as the gate on the six symbols leaving crossing-report.ts; knip.json's root workspace declares scripts/*.ts! entries with no includeEntryExports, so unused exports of entry files are never reported. Proven on the live tree: RatchetVerdict was exported, read by nothing, and knip was green (round 5 N1, reconfirmed round 6). So a leftover refuseGrowth/compareBaseline left DEFINED but unused would pass knip, pass typecheck, and — before the NUL fix — pass the grep. Compile errors catch every symbol still USED; nothing named in the plan caught what was left defined, commented, or written into a record file. Restated honestly in the final plan: the search and review are the gate, knip only must stay green.

The severity granularity was settled from live data and two candidate grains were rejected arithmetically, not by taste. Ruling E asked for 'the smallest thing that works' and explicitly said not to assume. Measured: per-rule-name alone fails because 8 of 9 crossing kinds are dirty in production and 0 of 9 in development, so world-qualification is forced; per-(rule, world) fails because 4 of its 8 production warn cells span two or three sibling work packages and hold 195 of 221 violations, so under Ruling E item 3 no sibling could flip anything until the last one landed. The chosen grain is the existing group key '<source> -> <target> [<kind>] <world>' — byte-for-byte what groupKey already emitted and what every warn line already printed, so the dial added no new vocabulary. 31 warn keys, all production; all 7 former development keys absent, hence at error.

Five founder rulings landed mid-run and four of them amended or withdrew an acceptance criterion of plan.md: A amended AC-2 (the AI-runtime door is production-only, so tools/eval/src/judges.ts is untouched and the rule is RELAXED in the development world rather than exempted per-file), C amended AC-3 and withdrew plan.md's own 'except where a founder ruling names the file and the reason' carve-out — withdrawn by the founder who would have had to sign it, on the stated grounds that one exception becomes twenty — D amended the out-of-scope boundary, E rewrote AC-4 and AC-5. Two of the five (A, E) were closed by CHANGING A RULE rather than adding an exception, which is what kept the zero-exception contract intact.
